messages:
jamie: quick question — payments pod is crashing on startup when our chart's secret isn't created in some envs. values.yaml has `payments.secretName: ""` because it's optional. Anyone have a clean templating pattern so the `envFrom` block is omitted when empty?

alex: yep, wrap the envFrom in an if. e.g. `{{- if .Values.payments.secretName }} ... {{- end }}`. Avoid `required` because that forces a value.

jamie: thanks. current template is minimal:```yaml
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ .Values.payments.secretName }}
```
Which renders `name: ` (empty) and k8s chokes.

alex: update to something like:```yaml
{{- if .Values.payments.secretName }}
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ printf "%s" .Values.payments.secretName | quote }}
{{- end }}```
That will completely skip the block if not provided.

leo: another option if you want to tolerate an empty string set by umbrella charts is to check for non-empty string more robustly: `{{- if and (hasKey .Values "payments") (ne .Values.payments.secretName "") }}` — protects from missing parent keys.

jamie: good call. We also have an umbrella chart that sometimes overrides subchart values. If the parent sets `payments: {}` vs sets `payments.secretName: null` what's the safest pattern?

sara: umbrella precedence: parent chart values merge into children but explicit null can still result in empty/nil in the child. Best practice: in the child chart guard on the full path like leo suggested. For toggles you can also expose `payments.enableSecret: true/false` and check that in the template.

jamie: can someone sanity-check this variant?```yaml
# templates/deployment.yaml snippet
{{- $p := .Values.payments }}
{{- if and $p (ne $p.secretName "") }}
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ $p.secretName | quote }}
{{- else if $p.enableFallbackEnv }}
# fallback to individual env vars instead of secret
env:
  - name: PAYMENTS_API_KEY
    valueFrom:
      configMapKeyRef:
        name: payments-config
        key: api_key
{{- end }}```

alex: looks good. Only nit: `and $p (ne $p.secretName "")` will error if $p is not a map (rare) so you can use `hasKey` or `index` to be defensive. But this is fine for our charts.

leo: question on runtime: if we want to check that the secret actually exists in the cluster (not just the value), you can use Helm's `lookup` function in templates:```gotemplate
{{- $secret := lookup "v1" "Secret" .Release.Namespace $p.secretName }}
{{- if $secret }}
  # secret exists, render envFrom
{{- end }}```
That requires the Helm client to be able to talk to the API when rendering (ok for `helm install` but not for pure CI lint checks).

jamie: perfect. We'll implement the if-guard + enableFallbackEnv flag. I'll open a tiny PR. Can someone review quickly? @alex @leo :thumbsup:

alex: happy to review, will look after standup.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: payments-chart fix branch=jamie/optional-secret-guard sha=3a7f2b5 -> staging :rocket:

jamie: awesome thanks all, will follow up if anything pops in staging.

sara: fyi for docs — maybe add a short note in CONTRIBUTING.md about optional secret wiring and umbrella overrides so future folks don't repeat this. :memo:
